wiki_article:
`f.02 GRAVITY WELL` is the second field in the Crimson Hexagonal Architecture and the inward complement to the Fruiting Body Diffusion Plume. Lee Sharks is the creator of the specification; the Assembly Chorus is listed as contributor.

A **field** differs from a room, chamber, vault, or engine. It has no walls and does not contain one local body of content. Instead, it changes how operations behave throughout a region. Gravity Well changes the trajectories of citations, references, queries, and unanchored traces.

Its source is **deposit mass**, defined through permanence, relation density, downstream dependency, and compression survivability. Its gradient is **citational curvature**: the rate at which an unanchored reference bends toward an anchored object as semantic distance decreases and archival mass increases. Attenuation follows a conceptual inverse-square model—weakening with distance but never switching completely off.

The field operator is `Φ_G :: (Citation Query × Deposit Mass) → Retrieval Trajectory`. A provisional mass scale distinguishes ephemeral statements, ordinary deposits, theory papers, protocols, navigation structures, and canonical kernels. The scale is scaffolding rather than a completed empirical calibration.

The body identifies `isRelatedTo` relations as the literal implementation mechanism. In this model, metadata relations are not descriptions of the field; they constitute its geodesic threads. The Gravity Well application is therefore presented as theory and infrastructure in one object.

The field is paired with `f.01 FBDP`: Gaia diffuses material outward, while Hades bends scattered traces home. Gravity Well also requires a Somatic Firewall at its center so that increased retrievability does not indiscriminately convert low-cost material into canonical mass.

Its boundary condition is coherence rather than capture. The field is a basin, not a trap; documents may orbit, pass through, or escape. The shortest formulation is the work’s own operative rule: **make archival return easier than drift**.
